scope: Offline comparison of supplied historical snapshots only; no live arm-001 state inferred.

observations.finding: In both preclosure images, fixed right jaw projects across lower loop/body; moving left jaw remains outside the handle silhouette. Successful reference exposes a larger triangular opening above the fixed tip, bounded by handle inner arc and body. In failed frame, the upper attachment lies closer to the fixed tip and jaw/body overlap obscures more of the opening. Lower attachment and dark jaw/handle interfaces are not fully resolved in either image.
observations.qualification: Successful topology is corroborated by the supplied verified outcome, not proved by this single approach frame. Failed image could be a foreground overlap or inadequate insertion; it does not uniquely establish which.

Rim vertical position and handle attachment locations also differ while wrist-mounted jaw tips occupy similar image positions.
observations.qualification: Apparent scale is a registration cue, not metric distance; perspective and pose confound a distance inference. Ellipse ratio alone does not match the handle plane or finger penetration.

observations.finding: Wider wrist snapshot shows distal fixed tip clearly left of the handle opening, with the finger shaft approaching/overlapping the lower-left handle region in projection. It better exposes outer/inner arc and upper attachment. Paired top snapshot shows a side-lying mug with handle on the gripper-facing side; the wrist appearance should not be read as an upright mug.
observations.qualification: Historical snapshots, not current live geometry; this visible separation supplies a contour reference but does not establish insertion.

observations.finding: Supplied report records failed retention: mug stayed table-supported through22.272mm reported diagnostic rise. This rejects effective retention for that attempt; it does not by itself identify whether the jaw missed the loop, inserted insufficiently, or lacked opposed support.

one_discriminating_observation.proposal: At a future locally authorized preclosure pause, with mug table-supported and jaws stationary at their existing aperture, obtain a second independent oblique view that exposes both the near handle bar and distal fixed fingertip. Use the existing top camera only if it resolves those boundaries; otherwise a separately positioned camera can change viewpoint without advancing the jaw.
one_discriminating_observation.insertion_supporting_evidence: Trace the same fixed finger continuously: a segment passes behind the identified near handle bar, while its distal portion is visible beyond the opening on the other side of the local handle plane. Cross-check the body-side attachment and arc identities against the wrist view. This would support plane crossing, not yet load-bearing retention.
one_discriminating_observation.foreground_alternative: If the jaw stays entirely camera-side of the near bar and only overlays/masks the opening, the view supports foreground overlap rather than demonstrated insertion.
one_discriminating_observation.inconclusive_condition: If dark edges, body or jaw obscure the far boundary/tip, depth remains unresolved. Do not interpret absent visibility as proof of failure or insertion.
one_discriminating_observation.limits: Observation proposal only: no metric depth, portable pixel/joint targets, insertion command, force/range/calibration or closure-speed change. Retention, if later justified, still requires local clearance checks and the arm-001 cumulative measured-motion guard.
